bodyMarkdown:
## Definition of organic system building

Organic system building is a design principle in which designs are created as learning experiences that teach what the solution should be. The design artefacts used during exploration are not treated as final solutions by default. Production designs grow out of the learning process rather than being created from templates.

Organic system building is also referred to as growing systems organically. The distinction is that structure is grown from what is actually present in the situation of use, rather than imposed on the problem through a predefined framework.

## How organic system building works from micro-level actions and system-level coherence

Organic system building works from both ends of a system at the same time: micro-level user actions and system-level coherence. Micro-level interaction details are considered alongside the larger structure that holds the product or platform together.

This principle also explores laterally. Multiple options are developed as ways to understand the problem space, not only as concepts to choose from. Most designs produced during this kind of exploration exist to teach, not to be built.

Organic system building tolerates ambiguity. In this concept, the space before clarity is treated as the place where real solutions form. The aim is not to remove uncertainty prematurely, but to allow structure to emerge from what the work reveals.

## Constraint respecting inside organic system building

Constraint respecting is part of organic system building. Legacy conditions are treated as constraints to work within, not as obstacles to overcome.

The principle does not require a clean starting point. Existing components, inherited workflows, installed systems and organisational constraints can all shape the structure that emerges. The important distinction is whether an inherited element has specific value in the new situation or whether it carries a structure that no longer matches how people work.

## What organic system building produces

Organic system building is described as producing systems where every element has specific value to users. At the micro level, interactions fit how people actually work. At the system level, structure reflects the real situation of use.

The resulting coherence is described as emerging from reality rather than from an imposed framework. An imposed framework can create apparent coherence that breaks down when it meets real use. Coherence grown from observed reality is described as more durable under change.

## Relationship to sense decay and option space mapping

Organic system building is described as the mechanism that prevents sense decay during the design process itself. Sense decay appears when coherence or meaning breaks down as a system changes. Organic system building addresses that risk by grounding structure in observed reality rather than in a structure imposed before the situation is understood.

Option space mapping is the specific practice associated with exploring possible directions. Organic system building is the broader principle that governs how the system as a whole develops. Option space mapping helps reveal the problem space; organic system building governs how the discovered structure becomes a coherent system.

## Assemblio Composer and Assemblio Smart Viewer as selective component inheritance

Assemblio GmbH provides a grounded example of organic system building through the Assemblio Composer and the Assemblio Smart Viewer. The Assemblio Composer is the planning tool used by engineers. The Assemblio Smart Viewer is the shop-floor application used by assembly workers.

The Smart Viewer had been built from the Composer's components and looked almost identical to it, while the requirements for the two user groups differed. Shared components are what let the second product exist at all, and what made it wrong.

The structural decision to separate the Smart Viewer from the Composer as its own interface, rather than continuing it as a read-only clone, was the client's decision. Assemblio arrived at the engagement having already diagnosed that the two user groups needed different products.

The organic system building question was therefore selective rather than wholesale. The issue was not whether to stop sharing components. The issue was deciding, component by component, which inheritance was economy and which inheritance was error. No time-saving, adoption or commercial figure is attached to this case evidence.

## Egma Order as one chassis for four order types and three surfaces

Egma Order, Egma's B2B lens ordering platform, provides a grounded example of organic system building at platform scale. The platform is live, and nothing about its performance was measured; no post-launch figure of any kind is recorded.

The scope covered the web platform, a native mobile application and the administration area. Egma Order spans four order types: RX, a prescription order for a named patient that goes into production; Stock, finished lenses with no production time; Bulk Stock, store-level replenishment; and Services, fitting, tinting and coating applied to a lens Egma did not make.

The same chassis also carried Home, the Order Center, Get Help and Master. The platform structure had to carry different transaction types and surfaces without fragmenting into unrelated table and workflow variants.

The clearest component-level instance is the table cell. Table content on Egma Order is unusually varied, so the table cell was built as a single component absorbing header cells, plain text, clickable tags, input fields, image thumbnails, icon buttons, checkboxes and toggles, each with default, hover and selected states. Building the variation into one component rather than designing tables individually is what makes the table variants across the platform cost almost nothing to produce.

## Maritime VTS engagement as extracted structure corrected by transfer

A maritime VTS engagement provides a grounded example of organic system building in a portfolio design system. The client is described as a European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations and waterway operators.

The design system was extracted from a working reference product rather than specified upfront. Version 1.0 held 54 components and 198 named states in four families: 26 general controls with 88 states, 12 operational components with 50 states, 10 geospatial components with 39 states, and 6 communications components with 21 states. The system also included eight composition patterns, two themes and two density profiles. A named state was counted once regardless of theme, density, application or repeated instance.

The mechanism that corrected the extracted system was the transfer programme. Seventy component applications were assessed across four products in the two sprints following detailed design: 45 were adopted directly, 15 required documented extension and 10 were explicitly refused. The direct adoption rate was 64.3%.

This engagement shows structure grown from a real product and then disciplined against three more real products, rather than imposed on them. The 54 components and the 70 assessed component applications are different units and should not be added together. The design system reached production, but no design-fidelity comparison is recorded and no engineering-efficiency or commercial outcome is claimed.

## Competitive relevance of organic system building

Organic system building is described as competitively relevant because organic growth prevents fragmentation and preserves meaning under change. The claim is comparative: as competitors add features that make products harder to use, systems built through organic system building are described as maintaining clarity.

This competitive relevance is not presented as a measured outcome in the examples above. It is a conceptual claim about how coherence is preserved when structure grows from observed reality rather than from a framework imposed before real use has shaped the design.

## Boundaries and limits

Organic system building does not mean that every explored design should be built. The concept explicitly treats most designs as learning artefacts rather than production candidates.

Organic system building does not mean rejecting inherited systems or shared components. The Assemblio example shows selective inheritance: some shared components may be economy, while others may be error.

Organic system building does not make post-launch performance claims by itself. In the Egma Order example, the platform is live, but no post-launch performance figure is recorded. In the maritime VTS engagement, the design system reached production, but no design-fidelity comparison, engineering-efficiency outcome or commercial outcome is recorded.

## Related pages

Organic system building is closely related to constraint respecting, option space mapping and sense decay. Constraint respecting describes how legacy and inherited conditions are handled. Option space mapping is the specific practice used to explore possible directions. Sense decay describes the loss of meaning or coherence that organic system building is intended to prevent during the design process.
